annotation.authors_or_issuer: Chang, V.; Kamanooru, M.R.; Darko, G.T.
key_provisions_or_claims: 52% of 60 survey respondents were not ready for fully automated surgery.
75% recommended surgeons monitor robots, with robots aiding rather than fully autonomous.
Surgeon substitution is not an ethical choice.
Robotic skills should be included in anesthetic and surgical training curricula and simulation.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper examining ethical concerns of replacing surgeons with autonomous surgical robots, using a literature review and an online survey of 60 participants. Most respondents opposed full automation and favored robots assisting under surgeon supervision, and the authors recommend adding such skills to training curricula.
annotation.title_clean: Ethical discussions for autonomous robotic surgeries
annotation.title_en: Ethical discussions for autonomous robotic surgeries
annotation.venue: Proceedings of SPIE vol. 12128 (2nd International Conference on Industrial IoT, Big Data, and Supply Chain)
